title: Students who have never enrolled
instructions:
## The question

The registry needs the **name** and **programme** of every student who has **no enrolment at all**, sorted by name.

The database has three tables: **students** (id, name, programme, level, hometown), **courses** (code, title, credits, lecturer) and **enrolments** (student_id, course_code, semester, mark). Marks can be NULL when a result is not yet in. Use the Tables panel to peek at the data.

## Do this

There are three ways; try at least two and see that they give the same rows:

- a subquery with `NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrolments)`;
- a correlated subquery with `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrolments e WHERE e.student_id = s.id)`;
- a `LEFT JOIN` to enrolments and `WHERE e.student_id IS NULL`.

The checker accepts any of them as long as the rows are right and the query uses a subquery or an outer join.

config.schema:
CREATE TABLE students (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  programme TEXT NOT NULL,
  level INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hometown TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE courses (
  code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  credits INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lecturer TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE enrolments (
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES students(id),
  course_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(code),
  semester TEXT NOT NULL,
  mark INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_code, semester)
);

hints: `WHERE s.id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrolments)` is the shortest.
With NOT EXISTS, the inner query refers to the outer row: `WHERE e.student_id = s.id`.
Only one student has never enrolled.
